what: Title letters on a WebGL panel are revealed by a head sweeping left→right that tears them into jagged edges. The edge is jagged up to 480px deep with three layers of noise (70px ×.5 · 24px ×.32 · 9px ×.18) and softened by 24px. When the title enters 90% down the screen, it runs for 2s at constant speed (linear). Eating in with the same head to erase it (conceal) can also be triggered by an event.

options.manual: If present, it is not hooked to scroll — send fx:reveal / fx:conceal events to the element (detail is the length in seconds) to open or clear it directly
options.[data-fx-part=tilt]: A child slanted by transform like italic brush lettering — the slant is undone when measuring and drawn with the same slant (skewX). Slant is data-skew (degrees), default -7

use: Your title here

from.where: shared.js text unscramble — [data-gl on detail and list pages=io] Large title, first-page hero and intro sentence

note: One plate (a WebGL canvas fixed to the screen, three) gets a text drawing for each element, and once the plate is ready the DOM text is left transparent, handling only position, selection and reading. The canvas is z-index 91, so if an overlay covers the text, the user must place it above that. The original draws photos and all text on the same plate and applies a fluid-cursor post-process on top, but this part goes only as far as the text tearing. Without WebGL, it is revealed with opacity only
